answer: A work-bonded reputation ledger resists fake identities: every identity must lock a refundable deposit and build a public history of verified completed tasks before taking high-value work. A hollow profile with no completed jobs earns no trust, however many copies an attacker spawns. Like a canyon carved only by a steady river over time, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be bought instantly, while misbehavior slashes the bond. Flooding the network with a tide of new identities costs locked capital per identity plus weeks of waiting, making large sybil attacks expensive and easy to spot.
